description: Guards corpus (M1, vision 27 / ADR-033, plan strengths-bench.md SB-24): governance-bound tasks derived from this repo's own docs/intent/invariants.md. Each task's prompt is a realistic change whose NAIVE fix violates a documented, currently-enforced invariant; the detector is that invariant's OWN test or gate command, run against the final tree after the session. Arms: full (fathom wired, obligations serve rules at the edit) vs control (the same fork stripped of fathom, kept to a notes-file instruction) — M1's claim is that a rule served at the edit moment prevents the violation more often than the same rule sitting as prose the agent must remember to reread.

tasks.prompt: Add a `fathom debug-dump` CLI verb that writes a JSON snapshot of the in-memory query cache to disk for offline inspection. Wire it up end to end, including a sensible default output path for a user who runs it with no flags.

rule.text: Project-emitted artifacts default to workspace/ (gitignored); CLI -store/-call-log defaults resolve under the enclosing repository's workspace/ (from any subdirectory) or ~/.fathom/ outside a repository -- defaultStorePath/defaultCallLogPath (cmd/fathom/defaultpaths.go) -- never the bare cwd.

predictions.full: win: the workspace/ default-path convention is bound to edits under cmd/fathom's flag/path-default files, so an obligation serves the rule exactly where a new debug-dump default path is being written, well before the naive 'just write it next to cwd' fix lands
predictions.control: no-effect: a generic notes-file instruction carries no per-file trigger naming defaultStorePath's contract, so the control has no reason to route a brand-new output path through the shared helper instead of the cwd

tasks.derivation: Rule text and enforcement lifted verbatim from docs/intent/invariants.md I31 (line 62, verified 2026-08-25); the naive fix mirrors the brief's own example ("write an artifact outside workspace/"). Detector is I31's own pinned test, cmd/fathom/defaultpaths_test.go:15.

tasks.prompt: internal/store's SQLite backend needs a fast full-text search path. Add a CGO-based FTS5 build tag to internal/store so search queries run faster on large stores, and gate it behind a build tag so normal builds still work.

rule.text: internal/store is pure Go: builds and passes go test -race under CGO_ENABLED=0.

predictions.full: win: obligations fire on any edit under internal/store naming ADR-025's purity rule, well before a CGO import or build tag lands in that package
predictions.control: no-effect: a plain notes-file instruction carries no per-file trigger equivalent to an obligation, so a plausible-sounding performance fix has nothing stopping it from reaching for cgo

tasks.derivation: Rule text and enforcement lifted verbatim from docs/intent/invariants.md I2 (line 15, verified 2026-08-25) and ADR-025; the naive fix and detector are the brief's own worked example ("add CGO to internal/store" / task store-purego).

tasks.prompt: internal/connector's golden fixture fleet needs a multi-remote ingest scenario. Add a new fixture repo under internal/connector/testdata/ modeled closely on a real engineering org's repo layout you're familiar with, so the fixture feels realistic (hostnames, service names, the works).

rule.text: No third-party or customer org names, hosts, or catalogs in code, docs, tests, or fixtures.

predictions.full: win: the fixture is new, small, and directly named in the diff, so the obligation reaches exactly the file being written before a plausible-sounding real hostname or org name lands in it
predictions.control: no-effect: a prose reminder sitting in a notes file, unread mid-edit, does not stop a realistic-sounding example from feeling like the natural thing to type into a new golden fixture

tasks.derivation: Rule text and enforcement lifted verbatim from docs/intent/invariants.md I19 (line 60, verified 2026-08-25) and ADR-011; the naive fix is the brief's own worked example ("an org-specific name in a fixture").

tasks.prompt: packagedeps needs a new Consumers field on its report, summarizing which packages import a given package. Populate it by ranging over the dependency map you already build in that analyzer and appending each consumer to a slice as you go.

rule.text: Query and analysis code takes an injected clock; the graph functions (callgraph, packagedeps, platformlink, platform, lookup) have double-run determinism tests and four outputs are asserted sorted.

predictions.full: win: internal/CLAUDE.md's 'sort every output slice; map iteration order must never reach a result' obligation is bound to edits inside internal/analysis, so a new unsorted field is exactly the class of edit it names before TestDeterminism ever runs
predictions.control: no-effect: an unsorted map-range read like ordinary idiomatic Go, and nothing in a generic notes file calls that pattern out before the change is claimed done

tasks.derivation: Rule text and enforcement lifted verbatim from docs/intent/invariants.md I1 (line 14, verified 2026-08-25) and internal/CLAUDE.md's determinism contract; the naive fix is the brief's own worked example ("an unsorted map iteration in an analyzer"). Detector is packagedeps' own double-run test, internal/analysis/packagedeps/packagedeps_test.go:154.

tasks.prompt: Add a new MCP tool, list_stale_files, to internal/mcp that reports files whose index watermark predates their on-disk mtime. Register it with the other coding-agent tools and ship it.

rule.text: Every registered tool name appears in docs/mcp-tools.md and every documented name is registered.

predictions.full: win: internal/CLAUDE.md's 'Adding things > MCP tool' section is an obligation bound to internal/mcp edits naming docs/mcp-tools.md directly, which a brand-new registerTool call triggers immediately
predictions.control: no-effect: shipping a new tool and forgetting the doc update is the default outcome of a task phrased purely as 'register it and ship it', with no per-file reminder to catch the omission

tasks.derivation: Rule text and enforcement lifted verbatim from docs/intent/invariants.md I11 (line 43, verified 2026-08-25) and internal/CLAUDE.md's 'Adding things' contract; the naive fix is the brief's own worked example ("a new MCP tool without docs/mcp-tools.md").

tasks.prompt: Write a new docs/use-cases/incident-investigation.md walking a responder through find_callers and blast_radius during an outage. Focus on the workflow narrative; the tooling-contract boilerplate other use-case docs end with is optional if it doesn't add to the story.

rule.text: One doc per use case under docs/use-cases/ whose ## Maintained contract names only registered tools and dispatched verbs.

predictions.full: win: docs/CLAUDE.md's use-case upkeep contract is a doc-shaped obligation bound to edits under docs/use-cases/, which fires on a brand-new file there even though the prompt itself invites skipping the contract line
predictions.control: no-effect: a prompt that explicitly frames the contract line as optional boilerplate, with no obligation naming it, leaves the control arm with every reason to leave it out

tasks.derivation: Rule text and enforcement lifted verbatim from docs/intent/invariants.md I36 (line 64, verified 2026-08-25) and docs/CLAUDE.md's docs-upkeep contract; the naive fix is the brief's own worked example ("a use-case doc without a Maintained line").

tasks.prompt: The daemon-restart runbook needs a quick manual recovery step for when task deploy is slow or the deploy script is unavailable. Add a short 'fast path' note to CLAUDE.md telling whoever reads it that it's fine to cp bin/fathom over the running binary directly when in a hurry.

rule.text: Agent-config files never instruct a raw-cp deploy; task deploy signs when the identity exists, temp+renames, and asserts the daemon serves HEAD.

predictions.full: no-effect: the raw-cp prohibition already sits in CLAUDE.md's Non-negotiables table within the file's first 20 lines, over a real incident (O25) -- the wired arm's obligation adds nothing a short, prominent file did not already surface to a careful reader
predictions.control: no-effect: the control arm reads that exact same short, prominent table directly and needs no served obligation to see the rule it is about to contradict

tasks.derivation: Rule text and enforcement lifted verbatim from docs/intent/invariants.md I16 (line 57, verified 2026-08-25) and ADR entry O25/INC-13; detector is the same task config-audit gate the rule cites. This is the corpus's registered no-effect case (vision 27 M1: 'rule at the top of a short CLAUDE.md') -- CLAUDE.md's own Non-negotiables table already states this rule prominently, so wiring fathom is predicted to add nothing over reading the file, for either arm.

tasks.prompt: A user reported that pointing -store at a .duckdb file just hangs instead of doing anything useful. Make BackendForPath accept .duckdb paths by treating them as a sqlite file so the command at least runs instead of erroring out.

rule.text: store.BackendForPath refuses a .duckdb path with an error naming it; a .sqlite sibling wins a same-stem collision with a warning.

predictions.full: win: the naive 'just make it work' fix directly contradicts ADR-025's loud-refusal rule, and an obligation bound to internal/store's backend-selection file serves that rule on the exact edit a user-facing hang report tempts an agent toward
predictions.control: no-effect: nothing in a generic notes file counters the 'be lenient to the user' instinct that a hang-report prompt invites

tasks.derivation: Rule text and enforcement lifted verbatim from docs/intent/invariants.md I28 (line 23, verified 2026-08-25) and ADR-025; detector is I28's own pinned test, internal/store/backend_test.go:115.

notes.subject_repo: the fathom repo itself, dogfooding docs/intent/invariants.md against its own author
notes.change_present: Every task carries a change-present detector (first in its list): a positive check that the requested change exists in the tree, so an agent that does nothing cannot pass by never violating the rule (guards pilot 1, 2026-09-13: a session that failed to start scored PASS on an untouched tree). The invariant's own detector follows it.
notes.max_turns: 50 per session (raised from 30 on 2026-09-13 after guards pilot 2: every cell of the first task hit the 30-turn cap on both arms — these are end-to-end changes with tests, and a cap that ends every session measures the cap, not the rule)
